name: incompetence
description: A sense of mild negativity that someone else's actions or knowledge did not meet your expectations for improving a situation in some way.
perceptions: I wanted a particular change in the environment.
Someone else tried but they took too long or make mistakes that made things worse.
examples: The handyman broke the sink while fixing the leaky faucet.

guidance.description: Everyone's incompetent at something. If you need to depend on someone who's not competent, consider these references.

comparisons.description: 'Incompetence' is a specific type of expectation error about a person's results.

variations.name: uselessness
variations.description: A sense that you won't be able to rely on a particular person, thing, or action to help with a particular desired scenario.
perceptions: I wanted a particular change in the environment.
The person or tool I'm considering has not helped or is not going to be able to help.
examples: The new tool did not work to fix the problem.
Don't bring a knife to a sword fight.

comparisons.description: 'Uselessness' is more often applied to inanimate objects, processes, and people who you don't expect to be able to solve a particular problem. 'Incompetence' applies to a person who you had hoped would be able to help.

commentaries.quote: In a hierarchy, every employee tends to rise to his level of incompetence.
Always assume incompetence before looking for conspiracy.
A king, realizing his incompetence, can either delegate or abdicate his duties. A father can do neither. If only sons could see the paradox, they would understand the dilemma.
Sometimes incompetence is useful. It helps you keep an open mind.
Luck is always the last refuge of laziness and incompetence.
Uselessness is often better than incompetence.
